title: Survey Export
description: Export format for survey definitions and collected responses.

surveyVersion.description: Read-only version written by the survey export (8 hex characters). Copied to baseVersion when updating the survey; create imports ignore it. Never write it in a new survey.

updateMode.description: Survey Update Mode: true makes the file an update of an existing survey (see references/task-update.md). An update file has only updateMode, baseVersion and questions.

baseVersion.description: Update files only: the surveyVersion of the export the update is made from. The importer refuses a mismatch.

questions.description: Ordered list of questions (and headers) that make up the survey.

groups.description: Optional list of question groups (report sections). Each group has an 'id' and a 'label'. Questions reference a group via their 'groupId'. Alternative to the per-question 'group' string form.

id.description: Group identifier, referenced by a question's 'groupId'.

label.description: Human-readable section heading shown in the report.

responses.description: List of individual survey responses. Each response is a flat key-value object where keys are question or row IDs.

participants.description: List of pre-loaded participants who will be invited to the survey. Each participant is a flat key-value object whose keys must reference 'system' or 'category' questions only — no survey-question keys (single/multiple/open/matrix). Used independently of 'responses'; a typical file uses one or the other, not both.

surveyMessages.description: Optional overrides for platform-level messages shown to respondents outside the question flow (thank-you screen, screened-out screen, etc.). When omitted, the platform shows its own defaults. All five message keys are optional; set only the ones you want to override.

surveyComplete.description: Thank-you screen shown after the respondent submits their final answer.

header.description: Large heading shown at the top of the screen.

footer.description: Smaller closing line below the body.

redirectURL.description: Full URL the respondent is redirected to after the thank-you screen renders. Omit unless explicitly requested.

screenedOut.description: Screen shown when a screenout item fires and the respondent is exited before completing.

invalidPassword.description: Screen shown when the respondent enters the wrong access password on a password-protected survey.

alreadyCompleted.description: Screen shown when the respondent returns to the survey after having already submitted a response.

surveyClosed.description: Screen shown when the respondent opens the link after fieldwork has been closed.

messages.description: Optional outbound email and SMS messages sent to participants — invitations, reminders, thank-yous, and notifications. Not the same as 'surveyMessages' (which is end-of-flow screens). See 'invitations.md' for full reference.

update.description: Update files only: what an entry does. action add | edit (only what changes) | replace (whole question) | move | remove (soft delete). See references/task-update.md.

change.description: edit/replace: the riskiest kind of change, text < order < additions < structure. Optional; the importer computes it and rejects an understated claim.

placeAfter.description: Id of the question to place this one after; null = first.

oldId.description: edit/replace: the question's previous id when renaming it.

note.description: Short description shown in the review dialog.

itemUpdate.description: Update files only: renames an answer or row (its previous id).

text.title: Text
text.description:
A text shown in the survey (format-questions.md 'Texts'). A plain string with the formatting tags <b> <i> <u> <a href> <ul><li>, '
' line breaks and {token}s: a bookmark {Q} / {Q.1} / {Q:3}, a participant field {First name}, {SPACE} / {EMPTY} / {Company name}, or a picture, video, sound or document link {url} / {url|text} (~/file = a file of the project's media library). An object only when a field needs settings ('fields') or the text is raw HTML code ('html').
The text, with {key} tokens for the fields in 'fields'.

html.description: Raw HTML code instead of 'text'. {tokens} work here too.

fields.description: The text's fields by key - a {key} token in the text shows the field.

textField.title: Text Field
textField.description: A field of a text object: a value from the survey, a picture, video, sound or link, or a conditional text. Any field can have a condition.

condition.description: The field is shown only when this expression is true (same syntax as condition.definition).

question.description: answer: the question or row id.

answer.description: answer: the id of an open answer whose typed text is shown; '0' = the question's own open answer. Omit for the selected answers' texts.

url.description: link / picture / video / sound: the URL; ~/file = a file of the project's media library.

text.description: conditionalText: the text shown. link: the link text. A plain string: formatting tags allowed, but {tokens} are not replaced and fields cannot be nested.

altText.description: picture / video / sound: the alternative text. A plain string; {tokens} are not replaced.

width.description: picture / video: width in pixels, or e.g. '50%'.

height.description: picture / video: height in pixels, or e.g. '50%'.

id.description: Unique identifier for the question (its client reference). Used as the key in response objects for non-matrix questions, and in expressions as {id}.

type.description: Question type controlling both rendering and response format. 'period' and 'categoryVariable' are calculated variables with generated answers.

layout.description: Optional, header items only. Written by the platform on export ('header'); never required when authoring.

text.description: Internal label used in reporting and data exports.

surveyText.description: Question text shown to respondents. Omitted for header and excluded questions.

comment.description: Additional instruction or sub-heading displayed beneath the question text.

group.description: Optional report section this question belongs to, given as a plain label string (e.g. 'About you'). The platform derives the set of groups from the distinct strings. Simplest form for authoring; do not combine with 'groupId' on the same question.

groupId.description: Optional reference to a top-level 'groups' entry by its 'id'. Use this form when groups are declared in the top-level 'groups' array; do not combine with 'group' on the same question.

excluded.description: When true the question is hidden from respondents - typically a calculated variable. Data is still present in responses. Default false, except on 'period' and 'categoryVariable' questions, which are hidden unless 'excluded': false.

calculated.description: Only for a calculated question that has no rules yet: keeps the method. A question whose answers (or rows) have 'calculation' is calculated without this key.

coded.description: Coded open ends: the values are produced by matching the source open answers against each answer's 'codes'. One source as a string, several as a list, or an object when matchMode or multipleCodes differ from their defaults. Sources are references: {Q}, {Grid}.N, {Q}:{0} (the question's own open answer), {Q}:{id} or {Q}:A<n> (one open answer).

sources.description: One source reference, or a list.

matchMode.description: Default 'search' (a code found anywhere in the text). 'exact': the whole text must equal a code.

multipleCodes.description: One text can get several codes. Default true on 'multiple', false on 'single'.

period.description: type='period': the period type as a string, or an object when another setting differs from its default.

periodBase.description: Default 'EventDate'. Response = response end time, ResponseStart = response start time.

category.description: type='categoryVariable': the category path (relative ids separated by ':') as a string, or an object when another setting differs from its default.

min.description: Minimum number of answers the respondent must select or provide.

max.description: Maximum number of answers the respondent may select or provide.

interface.description: Hint for the survey renderer on how to display answer options. Recommended: buttons, dropdown, vertical. Grid-only special interfaces (use only when explicitly requested): slider (single-select grid, or numeric open grid with minValue/maxValue), dragdrop (single-select grid, drag rows into one box per answer), ranking (single-select grid, drag rows into rank order; answers are the rank positions). Rare grid legends, not recommended: alpha (automatic A,B,C legend), numeric (automatic 1,2,3 legend).

placeholder.description: Empty-state prompt text. On a 'dropdown' interface this is the unselected placeholder row shown before the respondent picks an option (e.g. 'Select a country…'). Ignored on other interfaces.

noInterfaceValidation.description: When true, suppresses all advisory interface checks on this question: the long-label warning for interface='buttons', the recommendation to use 'buttons' for short/small answer sets, and the missing-placeholder reminder for dropdowns. Structural interface rules still apply. Set only when the chosen rendering is intentional.

randomAnswers.description: When true, answer options are presented in a randomised order to each respondent.

cssClass.description: Optional CSS class name(s) the renderer adds to this item's container, for layout/styling hooks. Space-separate multiple classes. Built-in: 'connectToPreviousItem' renders the item visually attached to the item before it (no section gap), e.g. a legal reference or note belonging to the previous question.

pagebreak.description: When true, a page break is inserted before this item in the rendered survey. Most commonly set on section headers so each section starts at the top of a new page, but valid on any item.

scale.description: Scale type. Set to 'Ordinal' on every question/grid whose answers form an ordered sequence; required when any answer is tagged Positive or Negative.

scaleLeft.description: Label for the low/negative end of a scale.

scaleRight.description: Label for the high/positive end of a scale.

scaleDK.description: Label for the 'don't know' or neutral anchor of a scale.

rows.description: Sub-items for matrix questions. Each row is answered independently using the shared answers list. Only present when the question acts as a matrix.

answers.description: Available answer options. Absent for 'header' type questions.

condition.description: Conditional display rule. The question is shown only when the rule evaluates to true based on prior responses.

label.description: Human-readable summary of the rule. Not evaluated.

definition.description: Expression evaluated against prior responses. Atoms have the form '{<QuestionId>}:{<AnswerId>}' (or '{<QuestionId>}.<RowNumber>:{<AnswerId>}' for matrix rows) and combine with 'OR' / 'AND' / 'NOT'. NOT is written directly before a parenthesis with no space: 'NOT({Gender}:{2})'. Example: '{Fulfilled}:{9} OR {Fulfilled}:{10} OR {Fulfilled}:{11}'. '[<QuestionId>]' or '[<QuestionId>.<RowNumber>]' in arithmetic position is the sum of answer points for that question, grid or grid row (e.g. '[Wellbeing] >= 10').

row.title: Matrix Row
row.description: A single statement or item within a matrix question. Responses are keyed by row ID.

id.description: Unique row identifier, normally '<QuestionId>.<RowNumber>' (e.g. 'Aspects.1'). A row exported with its own reference keeps that id (e.g. 'price'). Used as the key in response objects.

text.description: Row label shown to the respondent. Omitted when the question is a single Likert row (i.e. one scale without sub-items).

surveyText.description: Row text shown to respondents when it differs from the row label in 'text'.

calculation.description: A calculated grid row: a map from grid answer id to that answer's rule (see calculationRule).

calculated.description: Only for a calculated row that has no rules yet.

calculationRule.title: Calculation Rule
calculationRule.description: The rule of a calculated answer. Short form: a string - the condition (the answer is selected when it is true), or on an 'Open' answer its value. Long form: an object with 'condition' and/or 'value' ('value' only on 'Open' answers) and 'disabled'.

condition.description: The answer is selected when this expression is true.

value.description: Arithmetic expression: the value of an 'Open' answer.

disabled.description: true switches the rule off. Default false.

answer.title: Answer Option
answer.description: A selectable option, or the definition of an open-text input, within a question.

id.description: Numeric string identifier. Used as the value stored in response objects for closed questions.

type.description: Semantic classification of the answer. 'Open' marks a free-text input; 'Negative', 'Positive', and 'DontKnow' tag scale anchors for analysis.

connectedTo.description: For Open answers attached to a closed-list option (typically an 'Other / please specify' pattern). The value is the id of another answer within the same question; the open input is shown when that option is selected.

text.description: Display text shown on the answer button or label in the survey.

surveyText.description: Alternative text shown in the survey when it differs from the internal label.

symbolText.description: Short symbol or abbreviated label used in compact scale renderings (e.g. '0'–'10', '?').

dataType.description: Expected data type for open-text inputs. When absent the input accepts any string.

minValue.description: Lowest allowed value for a numeric (dataType 'integer') Open input. Required on a numeric slider grid (interface 'slider' on a type 'open' grid), where it is the slider's left end.

maxValue.description: Highest allowed value for a numeric (dataType 'integer') Open input. Required on a numeric slider grid, where it is the slider's right end.

charWidth.description: Suggested visible character width of the open-text input field.

charHeight.description: Suggested visible character height (rows) of the open-text input field.

placeholder.description: Placeholder text displayed inside an empty open-text input.

points.description: Points scored when this answer is selected (or, for an Open answer, when it is answered). Used by calculations and conditions via the '[QuestionId]' / '[QuestionId.RowNumber]' points reference, which sums the points of the respondent's answers. Default is 1 and is omitted from the JSON; only write it when the value differs from 1.

exclusive.description: When true on an answer in a multiple-choice question, selecting this option deselects all others. Standard usage: a 'Don't know' or 'None of the above' escape option. Write a boolean (as the platform exports); the legacy strings 'true'/'false' are still accepted.

codes.description: Coded question: the answer's match codes - comma-separated words or /regex/i patterns.

color.description: period / categoryVariable questions only: the report colour of a generated answer (e.g. '#e15759'). Such answers have only 'id' and 'color'.

response.title: Response
response.description: A single respondent's answers. Keys are question IDs (non-matrix) or row IDs (matrix rows). Values are always strings.

additionalProperties.description: Answer value. Format depends on question type: a single answer ID for 'single'; semicolon-separated answer IDs for 'multiple'; the literal text for 'open'.

message.title: Outbound Message
message.description: An outbound email or SMS message sent to participants. Field requirements depend on messageType; see invitations.md.

name.description: Internal label for the message (e.g. 'Email invitation', 'First reminder'). Not shown to participants.

sendType.description: When/who the message is sent to. 'invitation' = first send; 'reminder' = participants invited but not completed (auto-filtered); 'thanks' = participants who completed (auto-filtered); 'notification' = unconditional broadcast.

senderName.description: Display name shown as the sender (e.g. 'Acme HR', 'Johnny').

title.description: Large heading at the top of the email body — typically a greeting like 'Hi #FirstName#,'. Email only.

bodyBeforeLink.description: Main message text shown above the survey link button. Email only.

linkLabel.description: Text of the survey-link button. The link itself is the built-in #DsLink# token. Email only.

bodyAfterLink.description: Additional text shown below the survey-link button. Email only.

footer.description: Smaller footer text — typically opt-out language. Email only.

optOutLabel.description: Label for the unsubscribe link in the footer. Email only.

body.description: Full SMS body. Must contain #DsLink# somewhere. SMS only.

condition.description: Conditional send rule — only participants matching the condition receive this message. Atoms '{QuestionId}:{AnswerId}' combined with AND/OR and parentheses. No arithmetic, no comparisons.

label.description: Human-readable summary of the rule. Not evaluated.

definition.description: Expression of '{QuestionId}:{AnswerId}' atoms combined with AND / OR / parentheses.
